questions.q: Work present if there is-
questions.explain: Work is done when a force causes an object to move a certain distance in the direction of the force. Let's look at the options: A) Force: Just having a force isn't enough. Think of pushing a heavy wall. You're applying force, but the wall doesn't move, so no work is done. B) Energy: Energy is the ability to do work. It's related to work, but not the same thing. You need energy to do work, but energy itself isn't work. C) Friction: Friction is a force that opposes motion. Friction can cause work
